title: "Fitting and inference"
description: "Estimate parameters, inspect identification and restore a fitted model."
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(frpp)
```

## A small identifiable example

Unit-exponential residuals recover a Hawkes likelihood. With zero excitation,
only the baseline is identifiable: the decay rate has no effect. Fix the
excitation and decay parameters in this example.

```{r poisson-fit}
model <- fspec(
  methods::new("hspec", mu = 1, alpha = 0, beta = 1),
  residual_law(c(rate = 1), dresidual = stats::dexp))
dt <- c(0, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5)
fit <- ffit(model, dt, optimizer = "stats", lambda_component0 = 0,
  fixed = c(FALSE, TRUE, TRUE), control = list(reltol = 1e-12))
coef(fit)
```

There are three events in one unit of time; the baseline MLE is 3. The tighter
optimizer tolerance makes this example easier to compare with that analytic
answer; it does not validate inference for more complicated models.

## Optimizers and parameter sharing

The default `optimizer = "maxLik"` requires the optional maxLik package.
`optimizer = "stats"` uses R's `optim()` or `constrOptim()` through emhawkes,
without requiring maxLik. Controls differ: stats uses `control$maxit`, while
maxLik uses `control$iterlim`.

By default, equal starting values within a numeric matrix share a parameter.
Use `reduced = FALSE` for separate entries. Function parameters with the same
name remain shared. Inspect `coef(fit)` to see the resulting names and order
before specifying fixed parameters or constraints.

`constraint` and `constraints` are alternative spellings; supply one.
Linear inequalities use `list(ineqA = A, ineqB = B)` for
\(A\theta + B \geq 0\). Columns follow the full optimization parameter order,
including fixed coordinates. The stats constrained optimizer requires an
interior start and does not support equality constraints.

A `valid = function(param)` callback can reject invalid parameter proposals by
returning `FALSE`. Its errors propagate; it should be deterministic.

## Residual parameters and identification

Residual parameters are fixed by default. Set `estimate_residual = TRUE` to
include them in estimation. This requires an identifiable model.

For example, with zero excitation and exponential residuals of rate \(r\),
the event rate depends on the product \(r\mu\). Estimating both freely cannot
separate them. Fixing the residual rate or an appropriate kernel scale resolves
that particular ambiguity. The package does not automatically normalize an
arbitrary residual law or diagnose every form of nonidentification.

## Inspect the result

```{r diagnostics}
summary(fit)
fdiagnostics(fit)
vcov(fit)
c(AIC = AIC(fit), BIC = BIC(fit), events = nobs(fit))
```

`nobs()` excludes the initial row. AIC and BIC describe the fitted likelihood;
they do not establish that the model or its standard errors are appropriate.

`fdiagnostics()` reports convergence and Wald covariance availability.
Covariance is withheld on optimizer failure, unavailable or nonpositive
curvature, and detected constraint boundaries. A reported
`available_unvalidated` covariance has not been checked for finite-sample
confidence-interval coverage.

Weak identification, long-tailed estimates and nonsmooth residual densities
can make Wald intervals unreliable. The moving transition in `tzexp` deserves
particular care. Profile likelihood and bootstrap methods need separate
validation; they are not implemented by `ffit()`.

## Restore and reuse a fitted model

```{r restoration}
estimated <- fitted_fspec(fit)
initial <- finitial_state(fit)
replayed <- do.call(logLik, c(list(object = estimated, inter_arrival = dt), initial))
c(optimized = as.numeric(logLik(fit)), replayed = as.numeric(replayed))
```

`fitted(fit)` also returns the estimated model. `finitial_state()` describes the
start of the fitted observation window, not the state after the final event.
Continuing a path requires its terminal state.

Save results with `saveRDS()` and restore them with `readRDS()`. Captured
callback environments remain references to external state; saving a fit does
not automatically freeze that external state.
